editorial:
Imagine one of the biggest scandals in sports history, where a simple skating competition turned into a real-life crime drama. You get to dive deep into the rivalry between Nancy Kerrigan and Tonya Harding, two women who wanted the same gold medal but came from completely different worlds. This documentary feels more like a conversation with a friend who knows all the gossip, as Mary Carillo guides you through the chaos. It captures that wild 90s energy perfectly, making you feel like you are right there in the middle of the drama as the world watches these two fight for glory.

What really makes this special is getting to see both women speak for themselves in exclusive interviews. It is a fast ride that doesn't waste your time, though some parts feel a bit short because it was made for TV. If you love true crime or sports stories, you will find this super interesting. You should definitely try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture, or you can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. Adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is also a great move if you want to keep this piece of history.
endingExplained: The documentary wraps up by showing how the scandal changed both women's lives forever. You see how Nancy moved on to a more polished public image while Tonya became a permanent outcast in the skating world. It ends by reflecting on the cost of fame and the lasting damage caused by the attack. There is no happy ending for everyone, just a sobering look at how one bad decision ruined multiple careers.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true crime and Olympic history.
